problem: Kaplan–Yorke conjecture on the dimension of an attractor in terms of its Lyapunov exponents
missing_details: Ordering of Lyapunov exponents in descending order λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ … ≥ λₙ
Definition of the integer j as the largest index satisfying ∑_{i=1}^j λᵢ ≥ 0 and ∑_{i=1}^{j+1} λᵢ < 0
Precise formula for the conjectured dimension: D = j + (∑_{i=1}^j λᵢ)/|λ_{j+1}|
Specification that “dimension” refers to the Hausdorff (or fractal) dimension of the attractor
Assumption that the dynamical system is sufficiently smooth so that Lyapunov exponents exist for typical trajectories
Clarification whether the conjecture applies to discrete-time maps, continuous flows, or both
refined_question: Let A be a compact invariant attractor of a sufficiently smooth dynamical system (flow or map) in ℝⁿ whose Lyapunov exponents along a typical trajectory exist and can be ordered as λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ … ≥ λₙ. Define the integer j = max {k ∈ {1,…,n} : ∑_{i=1}^k λᵢ ≥ 0}. Let D_{KY} = j + (∑_{i=1}^j λᵢ)/|λ_{j+1}|. Does the Hausdorff dimension of A satisfy dim_H(A) = D_{KY}?
justification: The problem name indicates a conjecture relating an attractor’s dimension to its Lyapunov exponents but does not specify how exponents are ordered, how the index j is chosen, the exact formula for the conjectured dimension, the precise notion of attractor dimension, or the smoothness and type of dynamical system involved. These details are all present in the canonical statement on Wikipedia’s lead section, which defines λ₁ ≥ … ≥ λₙ, the choice of j, and the formula D = j + (∑₁^j λᵢ)/|λ_{j+1}|, and notes that it is intended as an estimate of the Hausdorff (or fractal) dimension of the attractor. The refined question gathers these prerequisites and frames the open conjecture as whether dim_H(A) equals the Kaplan–Yorke (Lyapunov) dimension D_{KY}.
